domains.accepted_requirement: A positive monotonic appointment_state_version is read under the appointment lock and advances on every committed appointment state change.

current_observations.fact: Appointment has no appointment_state_version or other explicit state-version column; created_at is the only timestamp in the class and is not an admissible substitute.
The exact migration lineage demonstrates additive-column representability without selecting the future column definition.

additive_requirements: explicit positive monotonic appointment state identity
advance on every committed appointment state change

domains.accepted_requirement: The completed private receipt binds operation, practice, target, actor, opaque session digest, idempotency identity, request digest, audit identity, pre/post state versions and canonical public response digest/bytes.

current_observations.fact: The idempotency model already represents practice, actor, operation, hashed key, request hash, response status/hash/JSON, target, audit and session-shaped correlation, but not pre/post state versions or a stored canonical-byte field.
Completion stores response JSON and its canonical hash then flushes; it does not store canonical response bytes or pre/post appointment versions.
The idempotency migration establishes a durable table, completed-response constraint, uniqueness and target/audit references, demonstrating additive receipt representability.
The public result envelope is closed and can remain unchanged while additional correlation stays private.

additive_requirements: stored canonical public response bytes or an exactly equivalent byte-preserving representation
completed-status constraints covering the full private receipt
deliberately_unselected: reuse versus replacement of existing session-shaped field

domains.accepted_requirement: One backend transaction holds practice then appointment then idempotency-record locks, validates target and current authority, and only then classifies or discloses replay/conflict.

current_observations.fact: The existing shared claim attempts an idempotency insert and then acquires only the idempotency row with with_for_update before classifying conflict or replay.
The appointment mapping has practice identity and an appointment primary key suitable for an ordered locked lookup, but this review does not select the query.
Status confirmation already requires the shared Idempotency-Key boundary and a typed confirmation/result envelope.

additive_requirements: target absence stop before idempotency access
current authority recheck before conflict/replay classification
no insert or receipt disclosure before the accepted preconditions

cross_domain_findings: All three semantic domains are physically representable only through additive schema/service architecture; none is already represented end to end.
Existing timestamps are operational metadata and cannot substitute for the monotonic appointment state identity.
Existing response JSON/hash and audit correlation are useful primitives but do not prove stored canonical-byte replay or complete private receipt correlation.
Existing with_for_update use proves a row-lock primitive, not the accepted practice-appointment-idempotency order or authority-first disclosure.
The exact migration set does not prove the full later model-to-migration lineage; a physical design must bind every selected field to an exact additive migration.
